newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Guilder rates rise further on rate hike worries.
newsitem.headline: Guilder rates rise further on rate hike worries.

text.p: Dutch money market rates extended gains on Wednesday as dealers remained nervous Germany may raise interest rates, which could spark other European rate rises.
Dealers said the firmer dollar versus the German mark and other European currencies could trigger a rate move by the Bundesbank on Thursday.

"I give it a 50/50 percent chance," said one dealer, but another said a rate hike would be against "all rules" as it did not fit in with Germany's aim to qualify for the European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"If Germany raises interest rates, other (European) countries have to follow," he said.

Some dealers said the Bundesbank could try another way to strengthen the mark versus the dollar. "The Bundesbank could also choose an intervention (selling) the dollar but then, Germany needs to work together with other European central banks," a dealer said.
The dollar was trading at 2.1230 guilders on Wednesday morning versus 2.1154 guilders on Tuesday.

On Tuesday, Germany's Ifo economic research institute said it could see the Bundesbank taking "small steps" to send a signal to currency markets if the dollar rose above 1.90 marks. It was trading at 1.8850 marks this morning.

Guilder deposits rose a few basis points this morning as a result of rate hike worries. Dealers said gains should be limited as some investors started to think a rate rise would be too severe for the market.
One-month deposits rose six basis points to 3.32 percent bid and three-month deposits added four basis points to 3.36 percent bid.
One-year deposits rose six basis points to 3.64 percent bid, almost 40 basis points higher than a month ago.
The guilder was slightly stronger versus the German mark at 112.625 per 100 marks from 112.64 on Tuesday.
